Used in the Constitution (5 parts) and some codes.
Primary higher division in most laws: Labour Law, Family Law, Penal Code.
Higher division WITHIN a chapter. NOT the basic unit — never confuse with Anglophone 'section'.

emiri_decree.label: Emiri Decree (Marsoom Amiri)
emiri_decree.note: Issued by Emir under Art. 70 (Shura not in session) or for executive/organisational matters. Force of law equal to enacted Laws.

ministerial_decision.label: Ministerial Decision (Qarar Wizari)
ministerial_decision.note: Ministerial implementing regulations. No separate number series from other ministerial decisions.

constitution.label: Permanent Constitution of Qatar

hierarchy.note: 5 parts: The State (1-17), Guiding Principles (18-33), Rights (34-58), Powers (59-140), Concluding (141-150).
Used only within Part Four (Organization of Powers): 5 chapters.

constitution.note: 150 articles continuous. Part Four subdivided into 5 chapters (General, Emir, Legislature, Executive, Judiciary). No schedules.

qfc_regulation.label: QFC Regulation
qfc_regulation.note: QFC instruments are drafted in English using English common law conventions. Section is the basic unit. Use jurisdiction code qa-qfc for FRBR URIs.

frbr.date_calendar_note: Gregorian year in FRBR URI (internationally conventional, matches Al Meezan English index and WIPO Lex). Hijri date stored as FRBRalias. [REQUIRES HUMAN SIGN-OFF — see unresolved ambiguity 1]

numbering.insertion_note: Civil law tradition uses wholesale article replacement. If insertion occurs, Arabic مكرر (mkarrar = repeated/bis) suffix expected, e.g., Article (5) mkarrar → art_5mkarrar.

structuring.prompt_additions: Qatar uses ARTICLE (مادة, maddah) as the basic unit — numbered continuously throughout the law. Chapter (باب, bab) and Section (فصل, fasl) are higher divisions ABOVE articles, not below them. Section is NOT the basic unit. Article numbers appear in parentheses in Qatari convention: 'Article (5)'. Source documents are in Arabic (RTL); English translations may exist but Arabic is authoritative. Paragraph subdivisions within articles use (1), (2) numbering; lettered items use (a), (b). Most short laws have no subdivisions within articles. The signature block (Emir's name, date) appears at the END of the document — model as <conclusions>, not <preamble>.

supranational_memberships.note: GCC Unified Laws require domestic transposition by Emiri Decree or Law to take effect. No automatic direct effect. Qatar has transposed GCC Trademark Law (Decree No. 7/2014), GCC Customs Law, and other GCC instruments.
UN Security Council Chapter VII resolutions are binding; implementation requires domestic legislation.
